events.title: Treaty of Utrecht Signed
events.description: On July 13, 1713, Britain, France and other European powers signed the Treaty of Utrecht, ending the War of the Spanish Succession. Among its terms, Spain ceded Gibraltar to Britain.
events.significance: The treaty reshaped the European balance of power. It also began Britain's long hold on Gibraltar, which it still holds today.

events.title: Northwest Ordinance Enacted
events.description: The Continental Congress passed the Northwest Ordinance on July 13, 1787. It set out how the Northwest Territory, north of the Ohio River, would be governed. It also created a path for new territories to become states.
events.significance: It became a model for how the United States expanded westward. It also restricted the spread of slavery in the territory.

events.title: New York City Draft Riots Begin
events.description: Opponents of Civil War conscription began three days of rioting in New York City on July 13, 1863. The unrest turned violent and was aimed heavily at Black residents.
events.significance: The riots are widely regarded as the worst civil disturbance in American history. They exposed deep social and racial tensions in the Union during the Civil War.

events.title: Live Aid Rocks the World
events.description: On July 13, 1985, the Live Aid benefit concerts took place in London and Philadelphia, with other venues such as Sydney and Moscow also taking part. Some of the biggest names in music performed to raise money for famine relief in Africa.
events.significance: Live Aid was a landmark in global broadcasting and charity fundraising. It showed that popular music could mobilize worldwide public attention and donations.
